summary: A `field`, `every` or `not-every` gate on a `resource/...` subject reads its path the same way whether the subject is pinned to a claim (`resource/NAME@CLAIM`, as a resource input is) or not: in the resource's facts first, then in the whole observation. Before, a pinned GitHub item needed `facts.state` and the same item unpinned needed `state`, and the other form stayed pending forever with no reason given. Both forms now pass on both. A gate that resolved before still resolves; the one difference is that a pinned gate on a top-level name such as `kind` reads a fact of that name first when the resource has one, as an unpinned gate already did. Fixes #4557.

replay.detail: No claim or projection replay; a pending gate is evaluated again on its next pass.

schema.detail: No table, file or schema change.

rules.detail: No checkpoint, retention or digest change.

compatibility.detail: Gate evaluation runs on the member that drives the run; no claim kind, field or wire capability changes. A gate on an older member keeps the old paths until it upgrades.

recovery.detail: Rolling back restores the old paths; a gate that passed meanwhile keeps its recorded result.
